ig_caption:
Kubernetes OOMKilled (exit code 137) explained in 40 seconds 💥

This pod restarted 4 times in one minute. The code is fine.
⚠️ the app loads a ~300 MB AI model
⚠️ the memory limit is 128Mi
→ the kernel kills it (OOMKilled, exit 137), Kubernetes restarts it, it loads again... and dies again (CrashLoopBackOff)

The fix:
✅ measure real usage (kubectl top pod: 313Mi)
✅ set the limit above it (512Mi)
✅ set a memory request so the scheduler reserves it

Memory over the limit is not slow. It's dead.

Save this before your next deploy 🔖 Follow for more Kubernetes breaks.

yt_title: Kubernetes OOMKilled exit code 137 explained and fixed #kubernetes
yt_description:
Real run on a local kind cluster:
- a pod that loads a ~300 MB model with a 128Mi memory limit: OOMKilled, exit code 137, 4 restarts in a minute, CrashLoopBackOff
- fix: measure with kubectl top (313Mi), set limits.memory above it (512Mi) and requests.memory (400Mi): Running, 0 restarts

How to debug: kubectl describe pod → Last State → Reason: OOMKilled.

Series: Kubernetes in production, what breaks (live). Follow for more.
